quotes.text: Without primary keys, Dataverse can't guarantee row level integrity. It can't tell whether an incoming row should insert or update.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in one breath why missing keys turn every import into a gamble.

quotes.text: Identity is not a column, it's a contract. The simple version is use surrogate keys for truth, alternate keys for convenience.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable rule of thumb for key design in Dataverse.

quotes.text: If the list is finite and has no metadata, use a choice. If it has properties, history, rules, or compliance flags, it's a table, therefore a lookup.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear decision rule between choice and lookup columns.

quotes.text: Referential integrity isn't optional housekeeping. It's the foundation. If a child requires a parent to make sense, make the relationship required and define cascade behavior.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States a concrete modeling recommendation against orphaned records.

quotes.text: Power apps doesn't fix spreadsheet thinking. Clear data modeling does. Keys, types and relationships turn chaos into a system.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the episode's core thesis.

takeaways: Keep the Dataverse GUID as primary key and define alternate keys on business fields so imports can resolve and upsert rows reliably.
Declare explicit data types and clean data in Power Query before import instead of trusting Excel formatting.
Replace repeated text with lookups to parent tables, load parents first and make critical relationships required to prevent orphans.
hook: Building a Power App straight from Excel feels fast, but it carries missing keys, mixed types and fake relationships into Dataverse. This episode walks makers and Power Platform teams through five failure patterns and a step-by-step remediation path. You learn how keys, types and relationships turn a fragile spreadsheet into a reliable data model.
